faqs.question: What does VZV DNA detection by real-time PCR - blood measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) DNA in your blood.

faqs.question: Why is VZV DNA detection by real-time PCR - blood done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose VZV infection • To assess treatment effectiveness • To identify the virus in patients with weakened immune systems

faqs.question: When is the VZV DNA detection test recommended, and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor might recommend this test if you have symptoms of VZV infection such as fever and rash or have been exposed to someone with chickenpox or shingles.

faqs.question: What if the results of the VZV DNA detection test are abnormal?
What to expect during the VZV DNA detection test?
faqs.answer: This test involves taking a small sample of your blood, usually from your arm, which is then sent to a lab for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the VZV DNA detection test?
faqs.answer: Inform your doctor of any medications you are taking as they may interfere with the test results. Also, let them know if you have any special requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the VZV DNA detection test?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside VZV DNA detection by real-time PCR - blood include VZV antibody testing to confirm prior exposure, and CSF analysis if the virus is suspected in the central nervous system.

faqs.question: What is VZV DNA detection by real-time PCR - blood also known as?
faqs.answer: VZV PCR or VZV Real-time PCR

faqs.question: What are chickenpox and shingles?
faqs.answer: Chickenpox is a highly contagious viral infection that causes red, itchy blisters all over the body. Shingles, also known as herpes zoster, is a painful rash caused by the reactivation of the chickenpox virus in people who have already had chickenpox.
